title: Grammar: Quantifiers — Few, A Few, Little, A Little, Many, Much, Plenty
grammarTip:
Исчисляемые vs неисчисляемые существительные:

ИСЧИСЛЯЕМЫЕ (Countable) — можно посчитать:
student/students · book/books · idea/ideas · mistake/mistakes
→ many · a few · fewer · several · a number of · each · every

НЕИСЧИСЛЯЕМЫЕ (Uncountable) — нельзя посчитать:
water · information · advice · knowledge · money · time · music · homework
→ much · a little · less · a great deal of · a small amount of

⚠️ Слова только с неисчисляемыми: much, less, a little
Слова только с исчисляемыми: many, fewer, a few, each, every
Слова с обоими: some, any, a lot of, lots of, plenty of, no

❌ "many informations" → ✅ "much information"
❌ "less students" → ✅ "fewer students"

grammarTable.subject: many
grammarTable.example: Many patients report improved sleep. How many tablets should I take?

grammarTable.subject: much
grammarTable.example: How much sleep do you get? She doesn't drink much coffee.

grammarTable.subject: few
grammarTable.example: Few doctors specialise in this area. (= not enough, a problem)

grammarTable.subject: a few
grammarTable.example: A few studies support this approach. (= some, which is encouraging)

grammarTable.subject: little
grammarTable.example: There is little evidence for this treatment. (= insufficient evidence)

grammarTable.subject: a little
grammarTable.example: A little exercise can make a big difference. (= some, which helps)

grammarExtra.title: Few vs A Few: Same Number, Different Attitude

rows.example: "Few people understand the full complexity of mental health." (= most don't — this is a problem)

rows.form: "A few" = positive — some, enough to matter
rows.example: "A few studies have shown promising results." (= some exist — this is encouraging)

rows.form: Test: can you replace with "hardly any" (few) or "some" (a few)?
rows.example: "Hardly any doctors" = few; "Some doctors" = a few.

grammarExtra.title: Little vs A Little: Same Amount, Different Attitude

rows.form: "Little" = negative — very small amount, almost none
rows.example: "Little progress has been made on this issue." (= not enough, disappointing)

rows.form: "A little" = positive — small amount, but it helps
rows.example: "A little stress can actually improve performance." (= some is beneficial)
"She was a little tired." "Take it a little more slowly."

grammarExtra.title: Many / Much: Questions and Formal Contexts

rows.form: Many and much are more formal; "a lot of" is informal
rows.example: "Many factors affect health." (formal) / "Lots of factors affect health." (informal)

rows.form: Much is mostly used in negatives and questions in spoken English
rows.example: "I don't have much time." "Do you eat much sugar?" (NOT: "I have much time." ❌)
"Too much stress causes burnout." "So many patients wait for treatment."

grammarExtra.title: Plenty of / A Great Deal of / A Large Number of

rows.example: "There is plenty of evidence that exercise reduces depression."

rows.form: "A great deal of" = a large amount (formal, uncountable)
rows.example: "A great deal of research has been conducted into sleep deprivation."
"A large number of studies support the benefits of meditation."
"The majority of patients responded positively to the treatment."

rows.form: ❌ How much patients visited the clinic?
rows.example: ✅ How many patients visited the clinic? (patients = countable)

rows.form: ❌ I have few money for the prescription.
rows.example: ✅ I have little money for the prescription. (money = uncountable)

rows.form: ❌ There is a little time left — we must hurry.
rows.example: ✅ There is little time left — we must hurry. (negative meaning: not enough)
✅ A little information was provided. / Some information was provided. (information = uncountable)

exercises.text: "There is ___ evidence to support this approach." (positive: some exists)
"___ doctors specialise in this rare condition — it's very hard to find one." (almost none, negative)
"How ___ sleep do most adults need? How ___ warning signs are there before burnout?"

opts: There is little progress in this area.
There is a little progress in this area.
There is few progress in this area.
There is a few progress in this area.
exercises.correct: There is little progress in this area.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct formal quantifier.
exercises.text: "___ research has been conducted into the link between loneliness and cardiovascular disease." (large formal amount, uncountable)
exercises.hint: "A great deal of" = large formal amount + uncountable noun

exercises.instruction: Which sentence has the correct positive meaning?
exercises.text: "___ exercise every day can significantly reduce anxiety."
exercises.hint: "A little" = small amount that has a positive effect

exercises.text: "___ people realise how serious sleep deprivation is — most underestimate its effects."
exercises.hint: "Few" = almost none = most people do NOT realise (negative)

exercises.text: "___ studies have confirmed the benefits of mindfulness." (formal, large number)
exercises.hint: "A large number of" = formal equivalent of "many"

exercises.text: "How ___ money is available for mental health services? There is very ___ — the system is underfunded."

exercises.instruction: Which sentence uses the quantifier to express a POSITIVE small amount?
opts: Little is known about this condition.
A few treatments have shown promise.
Little evidence exists for this claim.
exercises.correct: A few treatments have shown promise.
exercises.hint: "A few" = some treatments exist — this is positive/encouraging

exercises.text: "There is ___ evidence for the health benefits of social connection — this is a well-researched area." (more than enough)
"I have few patience for people who ignore medical advice."
"Too ___ stress causes physical illness. Too ___ responsibilities lead to the same result."

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct sentence for a formal report.
opts: Lots of people struggle with mental health.
A large number of individuals experience mental health difficulties.
So many people have mental health problems.
Heaps of research exists on this topic.
exercises.correct: A large number of individuals experience mental health difficulties.
exercises.hint: "A large number of individuals" = formal; "lots of/so many/heaps" are informal

exercises.text: "I know ___ people who exercise regularly. Sadly, most of my friends live quite sedentary lives." (positive: some exist)
exercises.hint: "A few" = some people — the speaker knows some, which is positive

exercises.instruction: Choose the sentence with the correct meaning.
exercises.text: "There is little hope for a quick resolution." means…
opts: There is some hope, which is good.
There is almost no hope — the situation is very difficult.
There are very few hopeful people.
exercises.correct: There is almost no hope — the situation is very difficult.

questions.text: "There is ___ research on the benefits of mindfulness — the evidence is clear." (large amount, positive)
"___ doctors work in rural areas — there is a serious shortage." (almost none, negative)
"___ exercise can help with mild depression — even a short walk makes a difference." (small amount, positive)
"How ___ time should we spend on screen-free activities?" (uncountable)
"___ studies have examined this specific population — more research is needed." (almost none, negative)
"A little progress has been made" means there has been almost no progress.
"___ funding is available for mental health services — this is a major crisis." (almost none, uncountable, negative)
"___ research has been conducted into this treatment." (large amount, formal, uncountable)
questions.hint: "A great deal of" = formal large amount + uncountable

questions.text: "___ people in this study had a history of serious illness — most were in good general health." (some, positive)

opts: There is little evidence for this claim.
I have few information about the treatment.
Much research remains to be done.
questions.correct: I have few information about the treatment.

questions.text: "___ patients responded well to the new treatment." (formal large number, countable)
questions.hint: "A large number of" = formal equivalent of "many"

questions.text: "There is ___ time to address the mental health crisis — we need to act urgently." (almost none)
